answer: A concrete mechanism can make fake identities expensive. Each identity must show a distinct capability profile across a horizon-indexed set of task families, and near-duplicate profiles are merged into one reward share. The basalt ledger of profile embeddings is public, while a walnut-marked set of clones collapses to a single seat. Faking diversity requires genuinely different competent behavior on unrelated tasks, which costs as much as running a real agent, so mass cloning loses its scale advantage.
